title: CS1 programming exercises with the Iris virtual tutor
summary: Students in three CS1 courses solve Artemis programming exercises with optional access to Iris, a context-aware tutor that reads the exercise statement, code, tests, and build output. Iris gives hints and counter-questions while withholding code and complete solutions.

sources.title: Iris: An AI-Driven Virtual Tutor For Computer Science Education
sources.evidence_quote: We surveyed students enrolled in three distinct CS1-level courses at the Technical University of Munich.

assessment.summary: Solve course programming exercises in Artemis while requesting context-aware tutoring when needed.
student_actions: Develop and submit code for programming exercises.
Review automated test and build feedback.
Ask Iris questions and use its hints to continue problem solving.

student_role.description: Students can ask Iris for private, exercise-aware support during practice and homework; instructors prohibit Iris in exams.

allowed_purposes: Clarify programming concepts and exercise issues
prohibited_actions: Receive code, pseudocode, concrete implementation steps, or complete solutions

assessment_system_role: Select relevant code and build context
